title: Programming
definition: Programming is the engineering activity of specifying, implementing, verifying, and maintaining executable solutions to defined problems.
purpose: Prevent programming from being reduced to typing syntax or accepting generated code.
history: Programming practice expanded from direct machine instruction entry to specification, implementation, verification, maintenance, and team delivery.
mental_model: Programming is a feedback loop from problem contract to implementation evidence and maintained behavior.
analogy: Constructing a bridge includes requirements, design, construction, inspection, and maintenance; the analogy stops where software can be copied and changed differently from physical structures.
real_world_usage: Turning a ticket into reviewed code and tests
common_mistakes: Treating generated code as completed engineering work
industry_notes: Professional programming includes review, testing, version control, deployment evidence, and change management.
ai_notes: AI can assist implementation, but the engineer retains responsibility for specification, verification, security, and maintenance.
interview_notes: Ask how the candidate would move from an ambiguous ticket to a verified change.
exercise_candidates: Label specification, implementation, verification, and maintenance activities
lab_candidates: Convert a bounded process into an inspectable programmed solution plan
project_candidates: Maintain a traceable change log for a tiny simulator
